messages.author: 2ef256a129b97763
messages.subject: what is RRO really about?
parts:
I have installed and dis-installed RRO on a couple of apple macs I have and listened to the webinar on the product.  I find RRO really interesting but I am still confused by what it is really about.
If I have to answer an elevator-type of question on RRO I would say in order (beyond the obvious source compatibility with R Cran):
1. It delivers intel MKL as open source on R
2. It provides a versioned package repository to increase stability and control with  mran.revolutionanalytics.com 
3. It allows to switch overnight to be under maintenance at a fee.

The problem is that since RRO launch few things have happened:
. The apple mac version was actually using the Accelerate Framework Reference, not MKL.
. As a developer of a (shiny) analytical application to use a versioned package repository is a big pain  in the butt: I need to be able to test betas of packages; install from github etc.  The situation may be different when I am going in production in a couple of months.

This means that RRO is "just" the ability to use RR support, provided that I use 1. and 2.  Correct?

On the other hand, is there a way to switch off sourcing packages from mran, and maybe go back to a versioned environment later (e.g. during the final steps of testing)?

Is there any plans to bring MKL to OSX in the future?

Many thanks!

Enzo

messages.author: 94c9ccb31cecffd1
messages.subject: Re: [RRO] what is RRO really about?
parts:
You are correct - see http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/news/#rro801:

  • The Mac build has been reconfigured to use the Mac Accelerate Framework for multi-threaded computations. This provides comparable performance to the Intel MKL. (Windows and Linux platforms continue to use Intel MKL.)

As for the package repository, you can switch to a different date, use a different repository (such as CRAN) or use checkpoint().  See http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/faq/#change-repos for details.
